cs.t: I wish I had more uses for my Casio calculator watch (CA53W). But these days it's faster to hold down the power button on my phone for half a second to activate a voice assistant. Now, if Casio made a smart watch that could run a micro-model on-device to do voice input for the calculator...

Just like the Nintendo Wii - graphics didn’t matter, it was just so entertaining! As a 10 year old I once played NUMBER INVADERS for 12 hours on my Casio calculator watch uninterrupted. My parents were very concerned :-)
cs.th: Space Invaders on your wrist: the glory years of Casio video game watches

cs.t: I have my TI 89 in my office by rarely use it. I wear a Casio calculator watch as my daily driver because i like the style and actually use the calculator function more often than you'd expect. I also have and learned to use a nice Japanese desk abacus, because it was fun.  And finally I own a giant novelty calculator for those big calculations.  Again, I never use them.
cs.th: Ask HN: Do you still use a hand held/desktop calculator?

cs.t: The battery of a 20$ Casio F-91W alone, will outlive several Apple watches.  While I'm with you in spirit, I'm not sure that's strictly accurate. The F-91W battery is rated for 10 years:  https://support.casio.com/storage/en/manual/pdf/EN/009/qw593...  The calculator version (which I use) is rated for three years, assuming you only let the alarm go off for 20 seconds per day, and use the calculator function for less than one hour per day:  https://support.casio.com/storage/en/manual/pdf/EN/009/qw320...
cs.th: Mechanical Apple Watch from Real E-Waste Apple Watch

cs.t: Or, just make devices not so power hungry. I got this fancy tire gauge+filler.  It uses a couple coin batteries.  They live around 6 months with it "off".  I use it a couple times a year, so basically every time I go to use it it is dead.  Removing the batteries requires disassembly.  A year or so ago I soldered in a couple AA batteries in place of the coin batteries, it's been good so far, but I'm waiting to see. On the other hand, I have a Mitutoyo caliper, which also uses a couple coin batteries.  I sometimes forget to turn it off when I put it back in the case, and so far, over 6+ months, it hasn't run the batteries out. So it  CAN  be done.  Both devices are basicaally the same: LCD display and they measure a sensor. Back when I was in HS, I had a Casio calculator watch, but it ate through batteries (3-6 months IIRC). The bracket for the strap broke, so I just taped it up in my locker.  Soldered it to a D battery, and never had to replace it again.  :-)
cs.th: Everything with a battery should have an off switch

cs.t: Hello Casio, Pac-Man calculator is nice and all but I have a simple idea that would be way more practical and useful and easy to implement. Simply build an inexpensive watch with a slot to hold a microSD memory card. Make it easy to strap a boatload of storage to your arm and take it with you wherever you go. That's it! Nobody does this ---- maybe just too simple and obvious? So I had to resort to building my own.  https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:6784665
cs.th: Casio retro Pac-Man calculator watch now available in US
